question: What will be the maximum intraday value of the VIX over these biweekly periods in Q3 2026? (Sep 7 - Sep 18)

calls.reasoning: Base: VIX closed 13.99 on Sep 4 2026 (2026 low), 9 trading sessions in window (Sep 7 is Labor Day). Reference class of 9-day windows starting from VIX 13-15 gives a median max/spot ratio near 1.17 with a fat right tail and a hard left floor (the window max cannot fall much below the start). Shifted modestly up for three in-window catalysts: Aug CPI Sep 11, a genuinely coin-flip FOMC Sep 15-16 where a 25bp hike is roughly priced against a hold, and quad witching Sep 18; plus documented Sep seasonality (median VIX 16.5 late-Aug to 18 mid-Sep since 1990) and steep contango signalling expected mean reversion upward. Held down by the observed calm regime (no VIX print above 21 since Jul 29) and the standard post-FOMC vol crush. Left tail truncated near 14.4 because Sep 8's high will start near current spot. Upper escape past 50 needs a 3.5x move in nine sessions from a quiet base - possible via a hawkish-hike shock into a 22x-earnings record-high market or a geopolitical event, priced at 1%. No lower escape: VIX has not printed below 10 since 2017-18 and the window max is anchored at ~14 on day one. No human prediction market on VIX levels found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold; the Kalshi Fed-decision contract is a different quantity and was used only as evidence on FOMC uncertainty.

Run 2 correctly notes Kalshi was not directly queryable, so 'no VIX contract on Kalshi' is unconfirmed-absent rather than confirmed-absent. No crowd anchor, no blend.
Unanimous across all three runs with the same named mechanisms; carried forward unchanged.

calls.reference_class: Rolling 9-trading-session windows of the CBOE VIX since 1990 conditioned on window-start spot <=15 with the term structure in contango, measured as max intraday high / starting spot; sub-conditioned on the window containing a scheduled FOMC decision and a CPI release.
